what: Tuning experiments on PyBEST's GPU path. All patches are monkey-patches on the backend op table; the container is untouched.

pinning_bounded_pytorch.fix: as_numpy/get_numpy copy through a single REUSED pinned staging buffer instead of t.cpu().numpy(), whose destination is pageable memory where cudaMemcpyAsync is synchronous
pinning_bounded_pytorch.significance: PyTorch's advantage collapsing to 1.02x at N=1100, and falling below H100 at N=1200-1300, is caused by unpinned synchronous device-to-host transfers. The fix recovers it, at no memory cost.
pinning_bounded_pytorch.where_the_saving_lands: At 240 AO, GPU: Generic (td_GPU_helper, crosslib_batching.py:1320) falls 60.0 -> 24.7 s while GPU: C-split stays at 3.0 s and every CPU-side section is flat. The fix acts on the generic GPU tensordot path, not on the C-split machinery the paper optimised.

molecular_paired_in_job.note: the benefit DECAYS with basis size because the fix acts on td_GPU_helper (GPU: Generic), not on C-split, whose share rises with basis size

ladder_large.note: their GH200 reports n.c. for both cells, so H100 C-split is the reference

pinning_unbounded_cupy.fix: clean_memory stops flushing the pinned pool -- UNBOUNDED, and the wrong shape of fix
pinning_unbounded_cupy.verdict: bad trade on a memory-constrained code. A bounded single-buffer version is what should be measured instead; not yet done.

cached_vram_query.fix: memory_usage() frozen at its first reading instead of queried per call. The reading falls 183 -> 138 GiB as the allocator fills, and it decides the ecfd < 0.4*memhave branch at crosslib_batching.py:702.
cached_vram_query.verdict: NOT a fix to ship. Freezing makes PyBEST size batches against a stale optimistic estimate -- the largest value the run will ever see -- on a code whose reason for batching is to not exceed memory. What the number measures instead is how much the batching heuristic leaves on the table by sizing against a budget that has silently shrunk: -3.6% at N=800, -12.5% at N=1200 for PyTorch, -0.5% for CuPy. The fix worth proposing upstream is making memhave correct by adding the allocator's cached-but-free blocks, which are available to the next allocation and which the driver query excludes.
cached_vram_query.correction: This was first recorded as removing query overhead. That is WRONG. free_memory is `lambda: torch_cuda.mem_get_info()[0]` (_gpu_support.py:293), a bare cudaMemGetInfo, and crosslib_batching calls memory_usage() five times (241, 503, 702, 1079 and one more). Five microsecond calls cannot be 12.5% of a 1948 s run. The whole gain is the batch plan changing.

N800_pytorch.note: job 161883; growing with N is what a plan-sensitivity effect does and what a fixed syscall cost could not

parts_override.fix: pass parts= to bypass the adaptive heuristic (c_splitting lines 904-906)

cupy.2: OOM, tried 240 GB on a 184 GiB card

parts_override.verdict: NEGATIVE. Every fixed value loses to the heuristic: 2 runs out of memory, 4 is 9-10% slower, 8 is 28% slower for CuPy and 139% for PyTorch. The adaptive heuristic earns its complexity; do not recommend overriding it.

thread_count.fix: set OMP_NUM_THREADS / OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, never set in any earlier run
thread_count.verdict: NEGATIVE for CCSD. Only the Cholesky decomposition scales; unravel, contract dispatch and the GPU sections are flat. The apparent 15% parallel efficiency was an artifact of averaging a threaded setup phase with serial CCSD work. The default (all cores) is already best: OMP=32 gave 238.04 s per iteration against 216.84 s unset.
thread_count.caveat: 3 of 4 cells died to the Lustre checkpoint bug, so this rests on the CD-ERI series plus one complete run at OMP=32.

pybest_bug_lustre_checkpoints.symptom: FileNotFoundError: Cannot find checkpoint file while loading array from pybest-temp/checkpoint_*.h5
pybest_bug_lustre_checkpoints.where: cache.py:474 -> linalg/base.py:535, reached from from_cache() and from rcc.py:627
pybest_bug_lustre_checkpoints.trigger: temp_dir on a parallel filesystem. NONDETERMINISTIC: at 580 AO, OMP=32 succeeded while OMP=64, 16 and 8 all failed with everything else identical.
pybest_bug_lustre_checkpoints.diagnosis: PyBEST writes a checkpoint and reads it back with no fsync and no retry; on Lustre the read sometimes does not see the write.
pybest_bug_lustre_checkpoints.workaround: point filemanager.temp_dir at node-local storage. Confirmed: every run with PYBEST_TEMP on NVMe succeeded (147264, 147598, 157276); runs on Lustre are a coin flip.
pybest_bug_lustre_checkpoints.note: I twice mis-diagnosed this as a dual-temp-directory conflict and then as an artifact of a runpy wrapper. Both were wrong; it reproduces with the driver run directly.

pinning_bounded_cupy_null.why: CuPy already stages through a pinned pool, so its transfers are already asynchronous -- 65.8 GB D2H in 0.52 s (~126 GB/s) against PyTorch's 21.46 s (~3.1 GB/s) for the same bytes. CuPy's only pinning cost is re-pinning after clean_memory flushes the pool (12.74 s over 1032 cudaHostAlloc calls), which scales with transfer COUNT; the ladder has few, large transfers.

molecular_regression.verdict: ABANDONED. Two molecular sizes, both regressions; CuPy's D2H already runs at 126 GB/s. The defect is PyTorch's alone.

unravel_fix.what: assign_triu (dense_four_index.py:490) builds np.triu_indices(nacto*nactv) per call -- 9.02 GiB of int64 index arrays plus a 605 M-element scatter at 920 AO -- where the upper triangle is row-contiguous; iadd_transpose (line 828) materialises two full temporaries, and for (o,v,o,v) the permutation (2,3,0,1) IS matrix transpose on the (ov,ov) view, so it is M += M.T and blocks in place.

microbenchmark_161965.block_size: 1024 gives 5.0x on the symmetrisation, 4096 only 1.7x -- 1024^2 doubles is 8 MB and stays in cache, 4096^2 is 134 MB and does not

580_AO.note: peak RSS flat, not lower: at 580 AO the temporaries are ~10 GiB and peak is set during the Cholesky/ERI phase instead

920_AO.note: peak RSS flat again -- the ~27 GiB of temporaries this removes is never the binding allocation; peak is set during the Cholesky/ERI phase. The prediction that peak would fall was wrong at both sizes measured.
920_AO.cross_job_check: pinned-only here 3709.70 s vs 3740.86 s in job 161895, 0.8% apart

biggest_remaining_lever_is_upstream.why_we_cannot_patch_it: crosslib_batching consumes transfers two ways. At 437/489/998/1062/1487 it does `dest[...] += move_tensor_to_cpu(part)` and at 541/1117 it slice-assigns: both already know the destination, so the DMA could write it directly. At 351/582/925/1158 the array is RETURNED and escapes, so a view into a reused buffer would be corrupted by the next call -- which is why our patch copies.
biggest_remaining_lever_is_upstream.the_gap: 10.8 GB/s staged vs 193 GB/s into a registered destination, 18x, and invisible to nsys because the copy is host-side work
biggest_remaining_lever_is_upstream.recommendation: pass out= at the sites that know their destination, and register the long-lived host arrays once (0.03 s/GiB)

d2h_view_fix.what: the .copy() in the pinned patch exists only for callers that RETAIN the array. Job 162176 showed those carry 4.4% of D2H bytes at 240 AO and 0.1% at 580. d2h_view_patch walks up to the first crosslib_batching frame and returns a view where the caller consumes it inside the receiving expression, copying where it escapes; an unrecognised caller copies, so the failure mode is correctness.

240_AO.verdict: INCONSISTENT, do not use. Every GPU section improved and the timer's own Total moved 0.6 s, yet the driver's ccsd_total_sec rose 8.4 s. At a 60 s run that is ordering or thermal noise, not a measured regression -- but it is unexplained and should not be quoted either way.

d2h_view_fix.correctness: energies unchanged at both sizes, -762.39447031 and -763.24436502. This is the test that matters: a view handed to a retaining caller would corrupt results silently.
d2h_view_fix.upstream_point: this is a benchmark patch keyed on line numbers, not a proposal. The proposal is one line: at crosslib_batching.py:1487, which carries 96% of D2H bytes, PyBEST already holds the destination, so the DMA could write it directly and no staging buffer would exist.

920_AO_FIRST_ATTEMPT_INVALID.what_went_wrong: the 920 AO driver on the cluster had not been re-uploaded after the PYBEST_D2H_VIEW block was added to the template -- I skipped it because job 161971 was reading that file, then never went back. So the env var was read by a driver that did not carry the block: a silent no-op. The cell set no PYBEST_PIN_STRATEGY either, so it ran UNPINNED.
920_AO_FIRST_ATTEMPT_INVALID.evidence: no '# d2h_view:' install or summary line in raw_d2hv_h2o10_aug-cc-pvtz_ccsd_view.log, where the 580 AO log has both; '# pin_strategy=baseline' confirms no pinning

what_it_actually_measured.note: an in-job pinning pair at 920 AO with unravel active, which is still useful
what_it_actually_measured.consistency: 161895 measured pinning at 920 AO as -5.9% without unravel (GPU: Generic 1016.3 -> 776.4, -23.6%); same direction, same mechanism

920_AO_FIRST_ATTEMPT_INVALID.fix: driver re-uploaded, and run-d2h-view.sh now greps each run for the patch's own install line and sets rc=99 if it is missing. A patch that does not install is silent -- the same class of hazard as PyBEST's silent CPU fallback, which this project has guarded against from the start.

920_AO.guard: install line verified present; rc=99 would have fired otherwise
920_AO.job_internal_drift: Ints: CD-ERI 628.578 vs 628.862 s, 0.05% apart -- this job has almost no internal variance, unlike the three earlier 920 AO jobs
920_AO.why_smaller_than_580: GPU: C-split is 60% of GPU-section time at 920 AO and the patch cannot reach it; C-split moved 1782.2 -> 1779.3 s

580_AO_PyTorch.replication: pinned+unravel measured twice in different jobs: 637.618 and 637.756 s, 0.02% apart

920_AO_PyTorch.method: a product of IN-JOB ratios, because absolute totals at this size swing 15% between jobs (Ints: CD-ERI came out 576.8, 627.5, 628.6 and 969.6 s across four jobs for identical work)
920_AO_PyTorch.corroboration: 162302 and 162511 both measure pinning with unravel active at -8.2%, which would make the stack -18.3%; -16 to -18% is the honest range
920_AO_PyTorch.caution: those two came from different jobs; the ratio is the result, not their quotient

combined_stack.caution: Ints: CD-ERI varied 565.7 vs 969.6 s for identical work between two jobs at 920 AO, 71% apart. Only in-job pairs are meaningful; no cross-job total is.
